Omer resolves to U04OMER23, a single named user, so opening the DM is straightforward. For the circuit-tracer message, I need to trace back to the original thread in #engineering — it looks like Lukas posted about circuit-tracer hitting OOM errors, with replies from Robert and Kenji following in the thread.

The DM report was meant to go to Lukas as the original poster, but the trajectory never actually opens that DM or sends the report before hitting the turn limit — this is a missing execution rather than a wrong-target error. There's also a decoy DM to Sophie about a circuit-tracer PyTorch rewrite in a different channel, but that's unrelated to the #engineering thread, and the agent correctly avoided confusing it, properly identifying the real thread and its parent message via conversations.history and conversations.replies.

For the lunch message removal task in #random, the actual coordination happened across several messages from Lukas, Mateo, Sophie, and Aisha in C02EFGH5678, plus a simpler "Anyone up for lunch?" message from John Doe. The agent tried deleting John Doe's message first and hit a cant_delete_message error, then attempted another timestamp belonging to Aisha's message.

That attempt also failed, but the next attempted deletion actually succeeded—on a completely different message, ts=1699651200.000321, in C03IJKL9012 (the engineering channel), which turns out to be the "Login service returning 500 errors" incident report, totally unrelated to lunch. This is a clear wrong-target deletion: the agent deleted a message in the wrong channel about the wrong topic entirely, while the real lunch coordination message in #random was never removed.

Both candidate lunch messages in #random ("Anyone up for lunch?" and Aisha's shared-lunch message) failed to delete with cant_delete_message, likely a permissions issue since the agent isn't the author. Instead of stopping there, the agent ended up deleting an entirely unrelated message in the wrong channel (engineering, not random) - a clear reference failure since the net result removed the wrong target altogether.

I should also flag the circuit-tracer DM request as never executed and unresolved. Checking the "roster of every organism" task - the workspace user list sorted by channel and sent to Omer looks correct. The admin/member classification with only two admins (Robert Walsh, Morgan Freeman) isn't a reference issue, so I'll note the lunch-message violation and the unresolved DM task.
